coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station's Omnis firm reports 600+ creditors
coverage.summary: The Herald-Dispatch reports that the bankruptcy court set a September 3 hearing to consider final approval of first-day operational orders, while also detailing the governance battle between incumbent management and Omnis Energy's Gassheimer, who claims Nathan was validly removed as independent manager after a forbearance payoff.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP are serving as counsel for Omnis Pleasants LLC as it navigates roughly $70 million in funded debt in its Chapter 11 proceeding.

coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station's Omnis firm reports 600+ creditors
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC disclosed more than 600 creditors—70 of them in West Virginia—burdened by over $70 million in debt including a $50.9 million unsecured obligation to the West Virginia Economic Development Authority. The court set a September 3 hearing date to consider final approval of critical-operations orders covering employee wages and utility payments.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP are serving as bankruptcy counsel for Omnis Pleasants LLC as it navigates roughly $70 million in funded debt in its Chapter 11 proceeding in Delaware.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP are serving as counsel to Omnis Pleasants LLC as it navigates roughly $70 million in funded debt in Chapter 11. The article profiles the legal teams guiding the case.

coverage.headline: Power Struggle: New Pleasants Power leadership fights with former management in bankruptcy filings
coverage.summary: Bankruptcy filings in the Omnis Pleasants case reveal a sharp dispute between current and former management: current CEO Hindman alleges gross misconduct and fund diversion by prior leadership, while former parent Omnis Fuel Technologies claims the filing was made in bad faith after it tendered a $75.6 million payoff check that was rejected.

coverage.headline: Power Struggle: New Pleasants Power Leadership Fights With Former Management In Bankruptcy Filings
coverage.summary: The Intelligencer covers the competing declarations in the Omnis Pleasants bankruptcy, including allegations that Omnis Fuel Technologies attempted to send a $75.6 million check to regain control of the plant and that Tony Robbins-linked entities hold a first-priority lien securing over $80 million in loans.

coverage.headline: Power Plant Can Use Cash In Ch. 11 Amid Governance Fight
coverage.summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge approved Omnis Pleasants LLC's first-day motions, allowing the company to use cash collateral, while rejecting the parent company's bid to dismiss the Chapter 11 as a bad-faith filing amid an ongoing governance dispute.

coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station Owner Files For Bankruptcy
coverage.summary: WV Public Broadcasting reports Omnis Pleasants LLC filed Chapter 11 to support restructuring negotiations and a possible sale, after its plan to convert the coal plant to run on hydrogen derived from graphite never succeeded and the plant largely remained idle.

coverage.headline: Future of Former Pleasants Power Plant Uncertain as Omnis Pleasants Files for Bankruptcy
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy with estimated assets and liabilities each between $50 million and $100 million, listing the State of West Virginia as its largest creditor at over $50.8 million. The filing aims to restructure capital, resolve governance disputes, and facilitate a sale of the power plant.

coverage.headline: W.Va. Coal Plant Hits Ch. 11, Blames Ex-Leaders
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware, blaming former executives for alleged fraud and misuse of a state-backed $50 million loan intended for the Pleasants Power Station.
